title: P11 follow-up: orthogonalize each attention head's Q, K and V Muon update separately (24 blocks of 32x256 instead of 3 of 256x256)
description: P11 follow-up (P02 family): split-QKV Muon now orthogonalizes each (role, head) 32x256 block of the QKV update separately instead of the whole 256x256 Q, K and V, with element RMS and total update norm unchanged. Every head then gets an equal-magnitude, full-rank-32 update each step, so no head's retrieval pattern is starved by the others' gradient directions, which should give the frozen RL stage more diverse, usable citation-lookup heads to build longer proofs from.
hypothesis: In whole-matrix orthogonalization, heads whose gradients share row-space directions with louder heads get a small share of the fixed unit-spectrum update, so some heads learn slowly or redundantly in the 4.7k-step budget. Per-head orthogonalization equalizes the update per head (each head's 32 singular values ~1), which should use all 40 heads' capacity and give a policy whose attention (premise/citation retrieval) extrapolates better to 7+ line proofs during expert iteration. Expected signature: pretraining steps and val loss within noise of 081 (the Gram matrices shrink to 32x32, so no step-time cost), and the gain, if any, in RL-solved and 7-10 line eval solves.
expected_delta: -35 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central -5: 081's 404 is probably seed-lucky, so even a real small gain may not clear it)

arch.change: none versus 081-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: per-head-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 081-claude except how QKV updates are split)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged from 081-claude: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized block: per-head Q/K/V blocks 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2, head (99,256) 1; every Muon update has element RMS ~1/16 times lr
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) are orthogonalized as 24 independent (32,256) per-head blocks; proj/fc1/fc2 and head whole.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: CHANGED: after elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each (768,256) QKV update to (24,32,256): one (32,256) block per (role, head), matching the fork's qkv(x).view(B,T,3,h,hd) row layout (row = role*256 + head*32 + j). Each block is independently Frobenius-normalized (x1.02) and gets five batched Polar Express steps (32x32 Gram, not transposed), then reshaped back. 081-claude used three (256,256) blocks (Q, K, V). Shape scale sqrt(max(32,256)/256) = 1, so element RMS stays ~1/16 and the total Frobenius norm of each Q/K/V update is unchanged (8 x sqrt(32) = 16 in quadrature); only its split across heads changes. proj/fc1/fc2/head unchanged (orthogonalized whole). No extra learning-rate multiplier; momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: unchanged from 081-claude: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2)
muon.normalization: unchanged from 081-claude: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6), now per (role, head) block for QKV
muon.local_check: CPU check against the pinned fork (ab629c7): reshape(24,32,256) block [role*8+head, j] equals weight row role*256+head*32+j; one muon_step on a random (768,256) gradient gives per-block singular values in [0.854,1.144] and element RMS 0.0632 (1/16 = 0.0625).

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 081-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 081-claude.
